title: Deviance from a pink noise regime in the temporal organization of semantic relations in psychosis
authors: Paola Moreno Ancalmo, Emre Bora, Rieke Roxanne Mülfarth, Svenja Seuffert, Tilo Kircher, Frederike Stein, Philipp Homan, Wolfram Hinzen
abstract: The notion of pink noise refers to 'scale-invariant' temporal dynamics, where fluctuations exhibit similar statistical structure across time scales. Departures from a regime associated with such scale-free organization toward uncorrelated 'white' noise or overly persistent 'brown' noise have been widely identified as markers of pathology across physiological and cognitive domains. Whether comparable alterations characterize the temporal organization of language remains largely unexplored. We address this question in the domain of psychosis, where language anomalies are pervasively documented. Specifically, we apply detrended fluctuation analysis (DFA) to quantify temporal scaling in BERT-derived continuous cosine-similarity time series capturing trajectories through semantic space, using clinical transcripts from patients and controls across three independent datasets. DFA scaling exponents were extracted to characterize the strength of long-range temporal correlations. Across all datasets, patients exhibited significantly elevated scaling exponents relative to controls, indicating abnormally strong long-range correlations with excessive persistence in semantic fluctuations. This temporal analysis opens a window into the multi-timescale organization of meaning as it unfolds in discourse. The results reveal a signature of altered temporal scaling in speech, consistent with deviations from criticality in physiological domains, paralleling known departures from criticality in brain function in psychosis and suggesting possible links between these two domains.
summary: This paper analyzes speech from psychosis patients by quantifying the temporal organization of semantic meaning using Detrended Fluctuation Analysis (DFA) on word embedding similarities. The authors found that patients exhibit abnormally high scaling exponents, suggesting excessive persistence and a departure from optimal 'critical' dynamics. This links linguistic pathology to known deviations from criticality observed in other complex physical systems.
main_problem: The study investigates whether deviations from a scale-invariant 'pink noise' regime characterize the temporal organization of semantic relations in psychosis, drawing parallels with pathology seen in other complex systems.
main_result: Patients exhibited significantly elevated DFA scaling exponents ($\alpha$) compared to controls, indicating abnormally strong and excessive long-range temporal correlations in their semantic fluctuations.
method: Detrended Fluctuation Analysis (DFA) was applied to continuous cosine-similarity time series derived from BERT embeddings of clinical speech transcripts.
model_or_system: The system analyzed is the temporal evolution of semantic relationships within human language production, modeled as trajectories through a high-dimensional semantic space using word embeddings.
key_observables: DFA scaling exponent ($\alpha$), which quantifies long-range temporal correlations; cosine similarity time series.
important_parameters: The critical regime (associated with pink noise/scale-invariance); the threshold for excessive persistence ($\alpha > 0.5$); minimum continuous stretch length (>100 words).
main_assumptions: That deviations from criticality in language dynamics mirror pathological departures observed in physiological or neural systems; that DFA is an appropriate tool to characterize multi-timescale organization of meaning.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows DFA scaling exponents ($\alpha$) across diagnostic groups (Zürich, Izmir, Marburg datasets); subsequent figures show partial Spearman correlations between $\alpha$ and symptom scores for different cohorts.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework by comparing noise regimes in pathology. It then details the application of DFA to semantic similarity time series from multiple clinical datasets (Zürich, Izmir, Marburg), presenting group comparisons and correlation analyses with symptom severity.
why_interesting: Although applied to linguistics, the methodology—using DFA to test for deviations from critical scaling ($\alpha$) in a complex temporal process—is directly relevant to characterizing non-equilibrium dynamics in open quantum systems or biological processes modeled by statistical physics.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
